instructions:
## Knowledge base

A knowledge base built from earlier debugging tasks is available at `/kb`. An agent like you wrote it. After each of those tasks it was shown how its answer had been graded and what the correct fix was, and it wrote with that in front of it. Those were different designs with different bugs, so judge for yourself what carries over to this one. It may be empty.

Look at it before you start work on the task, using the conventions below.

**Entries are skills.** A skill is a folder holding a `SKILL.md`, which begins with front matter giving a `name` and a one-line `description` and then sets out a procedure to follow; the folder may also hold scripts the procedure runs. Say when the skill applies, what to avoid, and which task it came from. Add or revise a skill only when a task taught you a procedure worth repeating.

**Skills live where the tool you are running in looks for them,** `~/.agents/skills`, one folder each. Their names and descriptions have already been listed in your context, and a skill's body is read when you choose to use it. To add or change a skill, write its folder there; a good description is what gets it chosen.

Follow the conventions you were given for what an entry is and how entries are arranged, and keep any index consistent with the entries. If the task taught you nothing worth keeping and the conventions do not require an entry, change nothing.
